module_title: Physical Divisions & Rivers of UP - Foundational Matrix (Terrains & The Twin Rivers)
introduction: Uttar Pradesh is predominantly a massive alluvial plain formed by the silt deposited by the Himalayan rivers. At this foundational level, you must master the state's three primary physical divisions and the exact entry and exit districts of its two lifeline rivers: the Ganga and the Yamuna.

core_concepts.title: The 3 Physical Divisions of UP
core_concepts.description:
1. **Bhabar and Terai Region (North):** The foothills of the Himalayas. Bhabar is made of porous pebbles/boulders (streams disappear here), while Terai is a marshy, damp, and highly fertile tract (famous for sugarcane and paddy).
2. **The Gangetic Plain (Central):** The largest physical division. Formed by rich alluvial soil. It is divided into Khadar (new, fertile alluvium) and Bangar (older alluvium).
3. **The Southern Plateau (Bundelkhand):** An extension of the Peninsular Plateau of India. Characterized by red, rocky soil, undulating topography, and water scarcity.

core_concepts.title: The Ganga River System in UP
core_concepts.description:
- **Origin:** Gangotri Glacier (Uttarakhand).
- **Entry District in UP:** **Bijnor**.
- **Exit District from UP:** **Ballia** (enters Bihar).
- **Major Cities on Banks:** Kanpur (the largest city on the Ganga), Varanasi, Ghazipur, Prayagraj.

core_concepts.title: The Yamuna River System in UP
core_concepts.description:
- **Origin:** Yamunotri Glacier (Bandarpunch peak, Uttarakhand).
- **Entry District in UP:** **Saharanpur** (at a place called Faizabad, not to be confused with Ayodhya).
- **Termination:** Merges with the Ganga at Triveni Sangam in Prayagraj.
- **Major Cities on Banks:** Agra, Mathura, Etawah, Hamirpur.

important_entities.name: The Ganga's Footprint in UP
important_entities.significance: The Ganga is India's longest river (2525 km). Out of this, its longest stretch lies in Uttar Pradesh, covering approximately **1450 km** and passing through **28 districts**.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.alert_title: The Bijnor vs. Saharanpur Entry Trap
trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation:
Examiners will always put both Bijnor and Saharanpur in the options to confuse you regarding river entry points. Memorize this firmly: 
- **Ganga** enters through **Bijnor**.
- **Yamuna** enters through **Saharanpur**.

mnemonics_and_tricks.memory_phrase: Ganga goes from B to B (Bijnor to Ballia).
mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: An incredibly simple phonetic link to remember the entry (Bijnor) and exit (Ballia) districts of the Ganga river in Uttar Pradesh.

exam_strategy_tips: In UP Police and UPSSSC exams, matching cities to their riverside locations is a staple. Remember that Lucknow is on the banks of the **Gomti**, NOT the Ganga or Yamuna. Gorakhpur is situated on the **Rapti**.
